────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Available now
  colonize         March a garrisoned land unit to an empty hex with intent=colonize to found a new settlement there.
  disband          Release units back to civilian population.
  load             Embark a land unit onto a ship in the same settlement.
  march            Order a garrisoned unit to march to a hex you have seen (live or remembered). A plain march leaves the unit standing where it arrives — that is how you gain ground you keep seeing; add stance "sentry" (or use `keryx unit post`) to post it as a forward watch. Intent "explore" is the opposite order: it may push into unseen land, but the unit turns for home the moment it arrives.
  post             March a land unit to a hex and hold it there as a forward watch — it stays (no patrol timer, no auto-return), extends your fog-of-war from where it stands, and intercepts enemy caravans within reach. It eats double grain in the field for as long as it holds.
  stance           Set or clear a unit's stance: "fortify" digs in and refuses to march, "storm" presses an assault, "sentry" stands watch — it spots foreign marches passing nearby and intercepts enemy caravans within reach. Note a unit does not need sentry to SEE: anything standing on the map already extends your fog-of-war. A unit already on the march can be given a stance too — a Runner has to catch up with it, and the stance bites where the unit stops.

Locked — here's how to unlock it
  build-road       Order an army to build one road edge between two neighbouring hexes. The stone leaves the nearest city when the order is given and travels as a caravan; building begins when the stone and the army are both at the first hex. Roads speed every traveller and anyone may use them; they never cross water or mountains and end at a river ford.
      ✓ a land unit to build
      ✗ 8 stone in this city (a plains edge) — 0 stone here
        → produce stone first (a quarry) — rougher ground costs more
  land             March a laden ship with intent=land to a hex of open, unclaimed land near the coast — it sails to the sea hex next to it, puts its cargo ashore there, optionally founds a colony on arrival (cargo_intent=colonize, no further order needed), and always sails home again on its own afterwards. Give the mission from port — a ship at sea takes no further orders.
      ✗ a laden ship garrisoned here — 0 laden ship(s) here
        → load a land unit onto a ship here first (`unit load`)
  recall           Send a recall order (by messenger) to a marching unit, turning it home.

        → march a unit first — recall only applies to units already in transit

Manage discrete military units

Usage:
  keryx unit [command]

Available Commands:
  build-road    Order an army to build one road edge between two neighbouring hexes
  list          List your units
  load          Embark a land unit onto a ship
  march         Order a unit to march to a hex — or explore, colonize or land (--intent)
  patrol        Post a ship on patrol at a coastal-sea hex (auto-returns after its patrol)
  pickup        Send a ship to fetch a unit standing in the field
  post          March a land unit to a hex and hold it there as a forward watch (no auto-return)
  recall        Recall a marching unit, or all marching units
  redirect      Redirect a marching unit to a new hex
  reinforce     Refill a thinned land cohort from its home city's growth
  repair        Repair a damaged ship's hull at a shipyard
  retreat-order Choose when a fighting unit retreats
  stance        Set or clear a unit's stance
  unload        Disembark the cargo unit from a ship

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for unit

Global Flags:
  -j, --json   output as JSON (for scripts and MCP)

Use "keryx unit [command] --help" for more information about a command.

Order a unit to march to a target hex (q,r coordinates).

Use --preview to estimate arrival without sending an order. The estimate uses
the current state; courier orders and unknown routes cannot promise an arrival.

Terrain passability:
  Impassable (all units):  mountain_limestone, mountain_red
  Land units only:         plains, hills, forest_olive_grove, forest_cedar,
                           scrub_maquis, semi_desert, river_valley, river_delta
  Naval units only:        coastal_sea, deep_sea, river
  Both land AND naval:     river_ford (the river's port — steep move cost for
                           either, but the one hex where a land unit can
                           cross and a ship can still sail through)
  (Land units cannot enter sea or river; naval units cannot enter land.
  river is impassable to land units — it is a wall, not a crossing. Every
  ~10 hexes of a river's length carries one river_ford instead.)

A newly recruited land cohort must finish gathering men and training before
it can march. Once ready, a cohort can still march after losing men; it does
not need to recover to 100 first.
A unit in fortify stance must be cleared (stance none) before marching.

Exploring: an explore order may target an area in fog. The server chooses
unseen reachable ground there and records what the unit sees along its route.
Run 'keryx map' to see the frontier coordinates.

--intent explore explores an area around the chosen hex for --ticks days.
It turns home by half the duration and reports what it saw on return. It needs
a reachable city of yours to return to. A land unit in the field receives the
order by Runner; a ship must be commanded in port. Works for land or naval
units. Omit --ticks for the server default; the server validates the range.

--intent land puts a laden ship's cargo ashore (megaron_plan_
skeppsuppdrag_landsatt.md R1): the ship must be a naval unit, in its own
port, carrying a land unit (keryx unit load first). --q/--r is the chosen
LAND hex, not a sea hex — the ship sails to the sea hex next to it,
lands the cargo there, and always sails home on its own afterwards. Add
--colonize to found a colony on arrival with no further order (--name to
name it). A ship at sea takes no orders at all (march/recall/stance) —
give every sea mission from port.

Ore on mountain terrain (copper, tin, silver):
  Mountains are impassable — you cannot colonize the mountain hex itself.
  Instead, colonize an ADJACENT passable hex: the ore deposit will fall in
  the new colony's catchment and can be mined from there.
  Use 'keryx map' to see which adjacent hexes are passable.

Conquest choice (--mode, only matters when the target is an enemy settlement):
  sack (default) — loot goods (silver + a share of the rest, weighted by
    portability) and raze the settlement; the loot is carried home as a
    physical, interceptable caravan. annex — keep today's behaviour: take
    the settlement outright (a captured capital becomes an ordinary colony).

Usage:
  keryx unit march [flags]

Examples:
  keryx unit march --unit <id> --q 5 --r -3
  keryx unit march --unit <id> --target 5,-3
  keryx unit march --unit <id> --q 5 --r -3 --stance fortify
  keryx unit march --unit <id> --q 5 --r -3 --intent colonize --name Thapsos --yes
  # Colonize the hex the unit already stands on (no coords needed):
  keryx unit march --unit <id> --intent colonize --name Thapsos --yes
  # Any march reveals fog along its route toward a frontier coordinate:
  keryx unit march --unit <id> --q 12 --r -8
  # Explore an area for 12 days, then automatically return home
  keryx unit march --unit <id> --q 12 --r -8 --intent explore --ticks 12
  # Land troops from a laden ship in port, then sail home on its own:
  keryx unit march --unit <ship-id> --q 20 --r -5 --intent land
  # ...and found a colony there with no further order:
  keryx unit march --unit <ship-id> --q 20 --r -5 --intent land --colonize --name Thapsos
  # Attack an enemy settlement and annex it instead of the sack default:
  keryx unit march --unit <id> --q 5 --r -3 --mode annex

Flags:
      --colonize        with --intent land: found a colony on arrival with no further order (use --name to name it)
  -h, --help            help for march
      --intent string   arrival intent: colonize (found a new colony — use --name to name it; omit --q/--r to colonize the hex the unit is on) | explore (explores the surrounding area, turns home by half the chosen duration; unit must be garrisoned at a settlement) | land (a laden ship in port lands its cargo on an unclaimed land hex, then sails home on its own; add --colonize to found a colony there)
      --mode string     conquest choice when attacking a settlement: sack (default, loot+raze) | annex (take the city)
      --name string     colony name (with --intent colonize, or --intent land --colonize)
      --preview         estimate arrival without sending an order
      --q int           target hex Q — axial coordinate, read it off 'keryx map' (required, unless colonizing in place or using --target)
      --r int           target hex R — axial coordinate, read it off 'keryx map' (required, unless colonizing in place or using --target)
      --stance string   stance on arrival: fortify|storm|sentry
      --target string   target hex as q,r — alternative to --q/--r (e.g. 5,-3)
      --ticks int       explore duration in days (omit for server default)
      --unit string     unit UUID (required)
      --yes             skip the colonize catchment-forecast confirmation (required for non-interactive/agent use)

Global Flags:
  -j, --json   output as JSON (for scripts and MCP)
